what_it_does: A microfluidic biochip is a tiny device — often used in medical diagnostics — that routes liquids through miniature channels to perform chemical or biological tests on-chip. Manufacturing defects (tiny blockages or dimensional errors in the channels) can cause the chip to malfunction, so designers want layouts that are as resistant to such defects as possible. While tools exist to measure how reliable a given layout is, there was no automated way to search for a better layout. AutoRE fills this gap by using Bayesian optimization — a smart, sample-efficient search strategy that builds a probabilistic model of which layout changes are most likely to help — to explore variations in channel sizes and positions without changing the overall connectivity. The result is a layout that is more likely to work correctly even when manufacturing is imperfect.
